digest.component_or_area: LLM verdict signing and provenance tracking
propositions: Signed verdicts currently record only a model string and cannot distinguish between verdicts served by different providers (e.g., Bedrock vs. Anthropic direct) or tiers, even though rebar signs all verdicts.

An additive provider_provenance object must be stamped into verdict payloads containing provider name, model, endpoint host, tier (first_class or best_effort), and the effective capabilities record, while preserving backward compatibility by leaving the existing model field unchanged.

The provenance record must be assembled in capabilities.py as a leaf module taking only primitives (provider, model, base_url, capabilities) to preserve module isolation, reusing the single capabilities record already computed per run rather than recomputing it.
Credentials in base_url must never appear in persisted payloads; urlparse().hostname (not .netloc) must be used to extract endpoint_host, stripping userinfo before serialization.
Verdicts signed on all tiers including best_effort (local development) to preserve the contributor on-ramp, with consumers able to reject off-tier verdicts via the tier field.

The provider_provenance field must be wired from runner step outputs through finalize_verdict into all three sidecar build_payload sites (plan_review, completion, code_review) to reach persisted signed payloads in production.
